pitch: The 14 principles behind Toyota's lasting success: philosophy, process, people and problem solving.
br: The right process: flow and rhythm
The right process: quality and standards
Principle 12: go and see for yourself
Solving a problem step by step
week by week · on the floor
quiz: According to Liker, why do most Toyota imitators fail?
They lack budget
They copy the tools without the philosophy or the culture
They have no robots
They produce too little
The tools are only the visible part; without long-term philosophy and a learning culture, the gains erode.
What are the four “Ps” of Liker's model?
Price, product, promotion, place
Philosophy, process, people, problem solving
Plan, pilot, performance, profit
Production, planning, personnel, permanence
Long-term philosophy, the right process, developing people and partners, and problem solving.
Why is continuous flow useful according to Liker?
It removes the need for standards
It makes problems visible by removing the inventory that hides them
It enables mass production
It reduces the number of customers
Like a river whose level is lowered: the rocks (problems) appear and must be removed.
What does the word “heijunka” mean?
Stopping the line
Leveling the workload in volume and variety
Critical reflection
Visiting the floor
Heijunka avoids surges: the steady tortoise rather than the hare.
What happens when an operator pulls the andon cord?
They are penalized
A team leader comes to help and the line may stop
Nothing, it's symbolic
The part is automatically scrapped
Jidoka: you stop to fix the problem at the source, and the operator is thanked.
What role does the standard play at Toyota?
A fixed rule imposed by engineers
The best known method today, the starting point for improvement
A document for auditors
A list of sanctions
Without a standard, you can't know whether a change improves things.
What does “genchi genbutsu” mean?
Decide quickly
Go and see the actual place, the actual thing
Cut costs
Train suppliers
Understanding a problem requires observing it on the floor, not only through reports.
What does the principle “decide slowly, implement fast” describe?
Delaying decisions out of caution
Preparing through consensus (nemawashi), then implementing quickly
Letting the boss decide alone
Testing every option in production
Prior consultation makes implementation fast because everyone understands and supports the decision.
